[[Minneapolis]], the largest city in [[Minnesota]], United States, and the county seat of [[Hennepin County]], operates under a [[Mayor–council government]] system. This article provides an overview of the structure and functions of Minneapolis's [[Local government|city government]].

==Charter and ordinances==
Minnesota was the fourth state in the U.S. to permit "[[Home rule in the United States|home rule]]" in 1896. A home rule charter serves as a constitution for a [[local government]]. It allows a community to establish and maintain a municipal corporation to provide for the common health, safety, and welfare.<ref name="Minneapolis 2015 i612">{{cite web | last=Minneapolis | first=City of | title=Charter History | website=City of Minneapolis | date=2015-01-01 | url=https://www.minneapolismn.gov/government/charter-and-code-of-ordinances/charter-history/ | access-date=2024-03-06}}</ref>

Several early attempts to establish a home rule charter in Minneapolis failed. In 1920, the matter was resolved by the [[Minnesota State Legislature]] when it codified the general [[Minnesota Statutes|statutes]] applicable to first class cities as well as all special laws specific to the City of Minneapolis at that time into the City’s first home rule charter. That charter remained in effect—through multiple amendments—until 2013, when a complete revision, including the incorporation of [[plain language]] principles, was adopted by voters in 2013.<ref name="Minneapolis 2015 i612" />

[[Local ordinance|Ordinance]]s are laws or regulations enacted by the city council designed to address the specific needs and concerns of Minneapolis, including zoning, public safety, noise control, and business regulation.<ref name="Municode Library g100">{{cite web | title=Municode Library | website=Municode Library | url=https://library.municode.com/mn/minneapolis/codes/code_of_ordinances | access-date=2024-03-06}}</ref>

==Structure ==
{{Further|Minneapolis City Council|List of mayors of Minneapolis}}
=== City Council ===
The [[Minneapolis City Council]] is the primary legislative body, consisting of members elected from 13 wards. The council holds significant power over local legislation, budget decisions, and oversight of city departments.

=== Mayor ===
The [[Mayor of Minneapolis]], currently a position held by a member of the [[Minnesota Democratic-Farmer-Labor Party]] (DFL), operates alongside the city council. The mayor's role was previously considered relatively weak compared to some other U.S. cities, but following a charter amendment in 2021, the mayor gained more power and the council was reduced to purely legislative duties. The mayor appoints heads of various city departments.

=== Departments ===

* [[Minneapolis Police Department]]
* [[Minneapolis Fire Department]]

=== Administrative bodies ===
The city administration also includes several independent boards responsible for parks, taxation, and public housing. These boards have the authority to levy taxes and fees within their respective areas, subject to limitations set by the Board of Estimate and Taxation.<ref>{{cite web |publisher=City of Minneapolis |title=City Council |url=http://www.ci.minneapolis.mn.us/council/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160207042452/http://www.ci.minneapolis.mn.us/council/ |archive-date=2016-02-07 }} and {{cite web |publisher=E-Democracy (e-democracy.org) |title=Minneapolis City Council candidates |url=http://www.e-democracy.org/wiki/Minneapolis_City_Council_candidates |date=October 26, 2005 |access-date=2007-03-24 |archive-date=2006-10-18 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20061018195829/http://www.e-democracy.org/wiki/Minneapolis_City_Council_candidates |url-status=live }} and {{cite journal |author=Anderson, G.R. == Political landscape and elections ==
Minneapolis is known as a stronghold for the DFL, reflecting a liberal-leaning political climate. The city council is predominantly composed of DFL members, with occasional representation from other parties such as the Green Party or the [[Democratic Socialists of America]].

==Neighborhoods==
{{Main|Neighborhoods of Minneapolis}}
The city is divided into communities, each containing neighborhoods. For example, the [[Near North, Minneapolis|Near North]] community is composed of the [[Hawthorne, Minneapolis|Hawthorne]], [[Jordan, Minneapolis|Jordan]], [[Near North (neighborhood), Minneapolis|Near North]], [[Sumner-Glenwood, Minneapolis|Sumner-Glenwood]] and Willard-Hay neighborhoods. Neighborhoods coordinate activities under the Neighborhood Revitalization Program. In some cases two or more neighborhoods act together under one organization.
